faqs.q: Where do families in Pembroke Pines give birth?
faqs.a: Most deliver at Memorial Hospital West on North Flamingo Road, right inside the city. It is the closest hospital with a full maternity program for nearly every Pembroke Pines address, and it runs the busiest Family Birthplace in the Memorial system. Families with high-risk pregnancies or a diagnosis that calls for the highest level of newborn care are often routed to Memorial Regional Hospital in Hollywood instead, about ten minutes northeast. A smaller number plan birth center or home births with midwives, the closest freestanding option being Natural BirthWorks in Margate.

faqs.q: Does Memorial Hospital West allow doulas?
faqs.a: Yes. Doulas are welcome as support persons at Memorial Hospital West, and it is common to see them working the halls of the Family Birthplace unit. Two of the doulas listed on this page have supported births there, which helps at check-in and triage. Confirm your support-person plan with your OB practice ahead of time so the labor and delivery team expects your doula, especially if visit policies have tightened since your last pregnancy.

faqs.q: How much does a doula cost in Pembroke Pines?
faqs.a: Birth doula packages in the Pembroke Pines and south Broward area generally run $900 to $2,400 depending on experience and what the package includes. Postpartum doula care usually bills hourly, and overnight newborn care is its own line item with some practices. Ask each provider what their fee covers, because prenatal visit counts and on-call windows vary. If the full package is out of reach, some South Florida doulas offer payment plans or reduced rates for Medicaid families.

faqs.q: Does Medicaid cover doulas in Pembroke Pines?
faqs.a: Yes. Florida Medicaid has covered doula services for eligible enrollees since July 1, 2024 under SB 264, including prenatal visits, labor support, and postpartum visits. In Broward County you are enrolled through a managed care plan, so call your plan and ask which enrolled doulas serve Pembroke Pines and how the referral works. The doula needs to be certified by an approved organization and enrolled as a Florida Medicaid provider.

faqs.q: Is there a birth center near Pembroke Pines?
faqs.a: Not in the city itself, but Natural BirthWorks in Margate is the closest freestanding midwifery birth center, about half an hour north. It offers birth center births, home births, and midwife-led prenatal care for families who plan a hospital delivery. For hospital-based care with midwife involvement, ask Memorial's maternity program or your OB about CNM coverage on the birth floor.

faqs.q: Which hospital has the best NICU coverage near Pembroke Pines?
faqs.a: Memorial Regional Hospital in Hollywood operates a Level IV NICU alongside Joe DiMaggio Children's Hospital, the highest neonatal care designation in Florida, and it is about ten minutes from Pembroke Pines. Memorial Hospital West carries a Level III NICU of its own, which covers the great majority of newborn complications without leaving the city. Most families never need to think about the difference, but it is worth knowing your safety net is staged this close.

faqs.q: Do Pembroke Pines doulas speak Spanish?
faqs.a: Several do. Natalie Grillo works bilingually in English and Spanish and offers lactation consultations in both, and the broader south Broward doula community reflects how diverse this city is. Ask about language when you book your consultation, since some practices bring in a bilingual team member for prenatal visits even when the primary doula works in English.
